content:
We've been on iOS 27 for about two months now. Of course, this is the beta version—the final version is still about four to six weeks away. That said, even though I've been running the beta on my own phone for the past two months, I haven't really felt its presence. It just... runs remarkably smoothly.

I still check in every few weeks, of course, and install the latest beta. That's the one constant of the entire iOS 27 beta experience.

Beyond that, I can't think of a single issue that people typically mention when talking about beta software. Basically no unusual battery drain, no overheating, no weird lag, and no random crashes.

You get all the benefits of this new system—Siri AI, the AirPods EQ equalizer, new digital wallet tickets in Safari, more powerful AI photo editing, and more—without any of the usual side effects of running cutting-edge test software. Honestly, that's quite rare.

iOS 26 itself wasn't exactly stable at launch, which may be part of the reason. Especially iOS 26.5 (at least for me) somehow made my phone keep respringing.

These are all personal anecdotes, of course, but ask anyone and you'll hear some story about iOS 26 acting up.

iOS 27 Overdelivers

That said, when it comes to speed improvements, bug fixes, stability, and quality-of-life improvements, iOS 27 has delivered some seriously impressive numbers. You might not notice at first because Siri AI is doing a lot of indexing in the background—though Apple recently rolled out iOS 26.6, which started kicking off Siri AI indexing in the background, so you won't have to wait when you upgrade to iOS 27. After that step, it's smooth sailing all the way.

I'm really looking forward to regular users being able to experience iOS 27 for themselves when the final version drops next month. It sounds hard to believe, but there's definitely a sense that Apple has fixed all of iOS's major annoyances. Of course, it's not perfect—software never is—but it's absolutely the best iPhone experience I can recall.

iOS 27 will support every iPhone model that iOS 26 supported, meaning the iPhone 11 and later will all get the update.
